headline: ELDORADO GOLD Q3 MISS: SKOURIES AISC HITS $2,050/OZ, FULL-YEAR GUIDANCE CUT UP TO 29%
snippet: Eldorado Gold (TSX: ELD) reported Q3 2026 production of 106,351 oz at an all-in sustaining cost of US$2,050/oz — up 22% from US$1,679/oz a year ago — as the Skouries mine in Greece ramps slower than modelled and lower-grade ore at Kisladag (Turkey) deepens the cost squeeze. Full-year guidance was cut to 425,000–475,000 oz including Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, versus the original 495,000–600,000 oz — a midpoint reduction of roughly 21–29%. Commercial production at both Skouries and McIlvenna Bay is pushed to late Q4. With gold near US$3,886 and AISC now above US$2,000/oz at one of its flagship assets, Eldorado's margin cushion has materially narrowed — incoming CEO Christian Milau acknowledged the ramp-up 'took longer and cost more than expected.'

headline: TECK Q3 BLOWOUT: EBITDA +97% TO $2.3B ON RECORD COPPER MARGINS — Unit Costs Hit $1.77/lb, EPS Doubles
snippet: Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.B) posted adjusted EBITDA of US$2.3 billion in Q3 2026 — up 97% year-over-year — as copper averaged US$6.40/lb during the quarter and net cash unit costs fell to US$1.77/lb (from US$2.09/lb a year ago). Adjusted profit attributable to shareholders reached US$923M (US$1.88/share), more than doubling the prior year's US$372M. Zinc also contributed strongly: gross profit before D&A of US$638M versus US$454M a year earlier, with a pre-tax impairment reversal of US$888M in that segment. The blowout results — released October 28-29 — underscore why copper-focused producers are delivering the sector's highest margins even as equity prices sold off alongside the broader metals complex in October.

headline: GLENCORE COBALT OUTPUT FELL 52% IN Q3 — DRC EXPORT QUOTAS FORCE STOCKPILE BUILD; COMPANY PIVOTS TO COPPER
snippet: Glencore's own-sourced cobalt output fell 52% year-over-year in Q3 2026 as the DRC government's export quota system — capped at 96,600 tonnes nationally for both 2026 and 2027 — forces the company to hold finished cobalt in-country rather than selling into the market. Glencore is now explicitly prioritizing copper at its Congolese operations, where higher copper grades and prices make it the more economically dominant metal. Cobalt produced above quota is building in inventory: Glencore expects to export 22,800 t this year and 18,800 t in 2027. S&P Global modelling cited by Semafor suggests the quota regime could push cobalt into a near-term deficit in 2027, potentially lifting prices and creating a re-rating catalyst for junior cobalt and battery-metals developers whose valuations have been depressed by multi-year oversupply.

headline: COPPER SET FOR FIRST MONTHLY LOSS SINCE JUNE — AI DEMAND DOUBTS WEIGH; CHILE OUTPUT FELL 15.1% IN SEPTEMBER
snippet: Benchmark LME copper finished October down approximately 2% — its first monthly loss since June — as investor uncertainty about AI data-centre spending growth weighed on the demand narrative that drove copper above US$7/lb earlier this year. Chile's September copper output came in at 387,870 tonnes, down 15.1% year-on-year due to operational weaknesses at major mines, adding to the long-term supply deficit case even as near-term macro headwinds pressure spot prices toward US$14,140/t. Chile's Cochilco separately raised its 2027 average copper price forecast to US$5.95/lb, acknowledging structural tightness below the surface of October's selloff.

headline: EQUITY AMPLIFICATION: SCCO -7.4%, FCX -5.5% VS COPPER -1.5% — Miners Pricing In Steeper Metal Decline Than Spot Shows
snippet: Major copper producer equities underperformed the metal itself by a factor of three to five in Friday's risk-off session: Southern Copper (NYSE: SCCO) fell 7.4% and Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) dropped 5.5% while LME copper itself declined only 1.5%. This equity amplification — miners falling roughly three to five times the commodity's move — typically signals either forced institutional selling and unwinding of over-leveraged positions, or a market view that current copper prices are unsustainable at elevated interest rates. For junior copper explorers on the TSXV and ASX, the same dynamic applies with added leverage: a simultaneous compression of commodity price expectations and equity risk premium produces outsized percentage declines.

headline: GOLD MINERS AT CHEAPEST VS S&P 500 IN 20 YEARS — Sector 19% Below NAV; Newmont Seen 34% Undervalued After October Carnage
snippet: Gold miners now trade at their cheapest valuation relative to the S&P 500 in approximately 20 years: the sector averages roughly 19% below estimated Net Asset Value (NAV), compared to the five-year historical average of approximately 0.95x for mid-tier producers. Senior producers trade at 0.92x P/NAV versus a 1.15x long-run average. The October selloff — gold -7.4%, GDX/GDXJ down further — pushed the sector into deeply oversold territory. Third-party intrinsic value models put Newmont near US$141/share versus a recent close near US$93-94, implying a potential 34% discount; Alamos Gold is at a 52-week low and approximately half its peak. Commerzbank analysts described the decline in precious metals as 'exaggerated' and maintained their recovery thesis. For contrarian junior mining investors, these multi-decade relative lows are historically the setup for outsized future returns — dependent entirely on a macro catalyst that eases rate-hike expectations.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,886, SILVER $49.78 ON HALLOWEEN — October Rout Extends Into Weekend; Monday Open Is the Next Catalyst
snippet: Gold traded around US$3,886–3,889/oz during Halloween weekend, down from the US$3,897 October 30 close, while silver held near US$49.78 — remaining below the US$50/oz level it lost earlier this week for the first time since November 2025. With October officially confirmed as gold's worst month since 2008 (-7.4%), the market enters a pivotal first week of November: the US midterm election on November 3 is the primary macro catalyst, with COMEX positioning remaining heavily short. Analysts broadly identify US$3,800 as the key support level dividing a year-end recovery scenario from a deeper selloff toward US$3,500; a Monday open above US$3,900 on constructive election polling would likely trigger meaningful short-covering.

headline: BANNERMAN ETANGO URANIUM MINE IN FULL CONSTRUCTION — Namibia's $353M Project Targets 2028 First Production; 750 Jobs Projected
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) and Chinese partner CNNC Overseas gave the green light to full-scale construction at the Etango-8 uranium project in Namibia following a final investment decision in mid-October, transitioning from early works into full mine construction with early-works progress reported as on-budget and on-schedule through Q3 2026. The US$353M project is debt-free: CNNC Overseas invested US$321.5 million for a 45% interest in the joint-venture company that owns 95% of Etango, with the remainder funded by Bannerman's A$124M equity raise. Designed for approximately 3.5 million lb U₃O₈ per year, Etango's offtake is aligned to CNNC's long-term nuclear fuel requirements — a supply-security model increasingly relevant as AI-driven power demand reinvigorates reactor construction pipelines globally.

headline: NEWMONT Q3 BEAT MEETS MACRO SELLOFF — $2.20 EPS vs $1.94 Expected, Yet Stock Down 5%+ in October
snippet: Newmont (NYSE: NEM) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of US$2.20 versus the US$1.94 consensus — a clean operational beat — yet the stock declined further in October as macro gold weakness dominated sentiment over company fundamentals. AISC guidance of approximately US$1,475/oz means Newmont earns approximately US$2,400/oz at current spot near US$3,886 — margins many analysts call among the widest in the company's 100-year history. The disconnect between operating performance and stock price reflects the sector's current rate-driven derating: gold miners being priced as rate-sensitive financial assets rather than commodity producers generating record free cash flow. The company expanded its buyback to US$6 billion in May 2026; at sub-US$95 share prices, that programme is purchasing shares at what several analysts describe as an extraordinary discount to intrinsic value.
